sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $105 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205].
Revenue grew 19.8% in FY2020, as a 19.3 percent comparable sales increase and new stores lifted sales [D183][P51].
Operating margin fell 4.9pp to 3.5% in FY2022, as markdowns, clearance and the cost of managing elevated inventory cut profitability [D290][F31][P38].
Revenue then fell 1.6% in FY2023 on sales declines in Discretionary categories, partly offset by growth in Frequency categories [D324][P30].
Food & beverage rose from 19.6% of revenue in FY2017 to 23.0% in FY2025 [D484][D506].
Home furnishings & décor sales fell from $20.3 billion in FY2021 to $15.6 billion in FY2025 [S29][S33].
Merchandise sales fell 2.0% in FY2025, a 2.0pp drag on revenue, as comparable sales dropped 2.6 percent on a 2.2 percent traffic decrease [D466][D467][P14].
Operating income compounded at 0.6% against revenue at 4.5%, so profit grew far more slowly than sales [F207][F205].
Diluted shares fell from 582.5 million to 455.6 million, so diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% against net income at 3.4% [X107][X116][F210][F208].
Operating margin of 4.9% in FY2025 sits below the 5.6% window median and the 8.4% high, but above the 3.5% low [F34][D590][D589][D588].
FY2025 operating margin fell 0.3pp, with cost of revenue subtracting 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D429][D440][D441].
The SG&A rate held at 20.6%, as a 0.6 point interchange fee settlement benefit offset 0.2 points of business transformation costs and deleverage on lower sales [D397][P11].
The filing excerpt gives the gross margin rate as 27.9 percent against 28.2 percent but does not state the cause in the passage cited [P12].
In FY2022 cost of revenue took 4.6pp and SG&A 0.3pp off operating margin, tied to markdowns and elevated inventory costs [D301][D302][P38].
Free cash flow of $2.84 billion was 0.77x net income in FY2025, below the 1.01x window median [F104][D405][D599].
Operating cash flow fell to $6.56 billion on lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [F84][P7].
Capex rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion on new stores and remodels, reaching 1.19x depreciation and amortization [D423][F94][P5][D406].
Free cash flow margin of 2.7% compares with a 4.5% window median [D401][D596].
Net debt narrowed to $4.30 billion in FY2025 from $10.6 billion in FY2022 [D410][D271].
Net cash of -4.1% of revenue ranks at the 50th percentile of six retail peers, whose median is -3.5% [D411][D612][D613].
Buybacks of $408 million and dividends of $2.05 billion took 86.8% of free cash flow in FY2025 [X126][X136][D413].
Return on average equity of 24.0% ranks at the 40th percentile of five peers, against a 28.6% median [D415][D616][D617].
Revenue declined in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, with FY2025 down 1.7% on comparable traffic down 2.2 percent [R1][D416][P14].
Free cash flow margin of 2.7% ranks at the 33rd percentile of six peers, below their 4.2% median, while payouts took 86.8% of free cash flow [D401][D610][D611][D413].
Operating margin fell in FY2024 and FY2025, 0.4pp in total, and operating income dropped 8.1% in FY2025 [R4][D383][D429][D417].
I dropped R2 because a 0.94x current ratio equals its window median, and R3 because the burn refers only to FY2022 [R2][F184][D602][R3].
Free cash flow margin below the FY2025 level of 2.7% while capex nears the roughly $5 billion guided for 2026 would show spending outrunning cash generation, in the FY2026 10-K [D401][P4].
Revenue growth above zero would break three years of decline, against FY2025 growth of -1.7%, in the FY2026 10-K [D416].
Operating margin recovering above the 5.6% window median would reverse the erosion from 4.9% in FY2025, while a lower reading would confirm it, in the FY2026 10-K [D590][F34].
